title: Oncall Handoff: Telemetry Annotations and Dashboard Stub Index
content:
Purpose:
This doc codifies a compact convention for annotating telemetry and dashboard panels to speed oncall handoffs for inference incidents. Focus is pragmatic: minimal fields in traces/metrics/panels that let an oncall engineer (or a triage bot) identify the dominant root-cause surface for token-serving latency, prefix-caching anomalies, and unexpected error-rate jumps.

Scope and intended users:
- Primary: ops/oncall, SRE rotation leads, and product engineers responding to latency/quality incidents.
- Secondary: feature owners and release engineers preparing rollouts that will be observed by oncall.
- Not in scope: full instrumentation curriculum or exhaustive metric cataloging; this is a short operational index and annotation guide.

High-level constraints (design goals):
1) Low cognitive load: each trace/metric/panel needs <=4 annotations to be useful in triage.
2) Cost-aware: avoid high-cardinality tags unless they are sampled or have explicit retention policy.
3) Robot-friendly: names and values should be parseable by automation (stable keys, limited vocabulary).
4) Backwards compatible: adopt alongside existing dashboards with incremental annotations.

1) Minimal metric definition set (for token-serving incidents)
- metric.name: token_latency.p50 | token_latency.p90 | token_latency.p99
  - description: end-to-end TTF (time-to-first-token) measured at API ingress; includes network and runtime queueing.
  - unit: milliseconds
  - annotation keys: panel_owner, model_family, cache_state (cold|warm), rollout_tag

- metric.name: kvcache.hit_rate
  - description: proportion of requests served from in-memory KV prefix cache vs persisted or cold path.
  - unit: ratio (0..1)
  - annotation keys: tenant_tier (free|paid|dedicated), sample_seed (for debugging sampled traces)

- metric.name: tokens.generated.per_second (per-node, aggregated)
  - description: throughput signal used to detect demand spikes and scaling anomalies
  - unit: tokens/s
  - annotation keys: autoscale_state (scaling|steady|throttled), model_variant

- metric.name: model.fallback.rate
  - description: ratio of requests that fell back to cheaper/older variant due to capacity/failure
  - unit: ratio
  - annotation keys: fallback_policy, affected_region

- metric.name: generation.error.rate (http 5xx, model timeouts)
  - description: counts and rates for internal errors that lead to customer-facing failures
  - unit: errors/minute and ratio
  - annotation keys: error_class (timeout|oom|rpc|model_error), last_deploy_tag

2) Trace annotation schema (compact, stable keys)
The trace span model should include a fixed set of attributes on the root span for easy correlation in dashboards and investigation tools. Keep each attribute low-cardinality. Suggested attributes (span.tags):
- span.tags.oncall_panel: short id of the dashboard panel that triggered an alert (e.g., PNL-45).
- span.tags.model_family: e.g., "llama-3a-70b", "redwood-clarity-13b" (keep family not exact commit to avoid noise).
- span.tags.cache_state: cold|warm|stale
- span.tags.routing_path: FAST_PATH|BATCHED|FANOUT
- span.tags.tenant_class: guest|standard|enterprise
- span.tags.kv_eviction_reason: memory_pressure|ttl|version_change|manual (optional, included for sampled spans)
- span.tags.rollout_cookie: canary|stable|rollback (helps tie to recent deploys)

Annotation best-practices:
- Use controlled vocabularies for cache_state, routing_path and tenant_class.
- Avoid embedding free-text error messages into tags; use error codes and store full error blob in logs only when sampled.
- When trace size/cost is a concern, send only the root span and a compact breadcrumb of downstream latencies (kernel, model, network).

3) Dashboard stub index and panel-annotation conventions
Every panel that participates in an oncall runbook should include (as panel metadata or a short title suffix):
- [OWNER: <github-handle>] - who to ping for first contact; prefixed owner handle allows automation to route messages.
- [TRACE: <root-attr-key>] - the canonical trace attribute that best correlates panel anomalies to traces. Example: [TRACE: model_family] or [TRACE: span.tags.oncall_panel].
- [SAMPLE: <rate>] - if panel relies on sampled traces, include the sample rate (1/100).
- [AFFECTS: <persona>] - e.g., trial-users, paid-users, dedicated (helps prioritize during incidents).

Panel title example:
Generate latency p90 — US-East — [OWNER: @rdesai] [TRACE: model_family] [SAMPLE: 1/200] [AFFECTS: trial-users]

Operator stub index (compact mapping for first-response)
- Panel: Generate latency p90 — US-East
  - Quick checks: Check autoscale_state, node_cpu, kvcache.hit_rate last 10m.
  - Trace anchor: model_family + cache_state
  - Likely causes: cold KV cache, scale lag, recent model warmup
  - Command snippets: 
    - curl "https://obs-api/metrics?name=kvcache.hit_rate&region=us-east&window=10m"
    - tracer.search("model_family:llama-3a-70b cache_state:cold", limit=50)

- Panel: Model fallback rate — global
  - Quick checks: model.fallback.rate by region, last_deploy_tag, capacity_pool_utilization
  - Trace anchor: rollout_cookie, affected_region
  - Likely causes: capacity pressure in committed pool, misconfigured fallback policy

- Panel: Error rate — generation errors
  - Quick checks: error_class breakdown, recent gitops deploys, queue_depth per node
  - Trace anchor: span.tags.error_class
  - Likely causes: model OOM after quantization change, RPC timeouts, bad prompt triggers

4) Lightweight dashboard widgets and drill paths
Guidance for building compact widgets that are useful to oncall:
- Keep widget queries under 150ms execution for the primary view; heavy aggregations should be behind a secondary drill link.
- Always offer a single-click "open traces" that pre-filters traces using the panel's canonical trace attribute and the panel's time window.
- Provide a minimal "what changed" snapshot at the top of the panel: last_deploy_tag, config_hash, and relevant rollout_cookie.
- Include a small column with "triage hints" for each row in table widgets (one sentence). These are static text on the dashboard metadata, not freeform.

5) Oncall handoff checklist (2-min version)
- Confirm alert scope: single-region vs global.
- Check panel metadata: owner, trace key, sample rate.
- Run quick checks listed in the panel stub (kv hit rate, autoscale state, fallback rate).
- Open traces pre-filtered by the panel's trace anchor and check root span attributes.
- If obvious cause: annotate incident with hypothesized cause and action taken, then close or escalate.

6) Retention and sampling guidance
- Root-level span attributes stored for 30d across all traces.
- Full trace retention for sampled spans only (default sample 1/200 for non-enterprise tenants, 1/50 for dedicated).
- High-cardinality attributes (user_id, exact_prompt_hash) must never be stored on root tags; place them in sampled payloads only.

7) Quick adoption plan (practical steps)
- Week 0: Add panel metadata fields to top 50 oncall panels (owner, trace key, sample rate).
- Week 1–2: Instrument root span attributes in runtime (span.tags.*). Start with model_family, cache_state, routing_path.
- Week 3: Build single-click trace drill links for the annotated panels and test with the oncall rotation in a tabletop drill.
- Week 4+: Iterate: add per-panel triage hints based on incident postmortems.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- How do we standardize owner handles across teams? (proposal: git handles enforced by dashboard linter).
- Sampling budgets vs visibility for high-traffic tenants — need a quota calculator for sampled traces.
- Should rollout_cookie be populated automatically by the deployment pipeline or left to application runtime? We prefer pipeline-populated labels.

Appendix: short glossary and common commands
- trace anchor: the trace attribute used to pre-filter traces for a given panel.
- sample_seed: small integer attached to some spans to make deterministic sampling easier during replay.

Common commands (examples):
- metrics quick: obs query --name token_latency.p90 --region us-east --window 5m
- trace drill: obs trace-search --filter "model_family:llama-3a-70b cache_state:cold" --limit 40

Notes and next steps:
- Ping @rdesai to add owner handles to the ops dashboard; @morganlee to scope the 50-panel list.
- Draft a dashboard-linter rule to enforce presence of [TRACE:] and [OWNER:] metadata on alerting panels (Jira OPS-3482).
